🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Tom Skerritt, the Emmy-winning actor known as Viper in "Top Gun," Captain Dallas in "Alien," Drum Eatenton in "Steel Magnolias" and Sheriff Jimmy Brock on TV's "Picket Fences," has died at 93.

Skerritt's family confirmed his death in a statement to PEOPLE. He died of natural causes on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.

"Our family is deeply saddened to share that Tom Skerritt passed away on October 21, 2026, from natural causes," the family said. "While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humor, curiosity, wisdom, generosity, and the love he brought into our lives."

Born August 25, 1933, in Detroit, Skerritt served in the U.S. Air Force as a classification specialist before turning to acting. His career spanned more than five decades, from an early breakout in "M*A*S*H" (1970) to "Alien" (1979), "Top Gun" (1986) — where he played the veteran instructor Viper opposite Tom Cruise's Maverick — "Steel Magnolias" (1989) and "A River Runs Through It" (1992).

On television, he is best remembered as Sheriff Jimmy Brock on the David E. Kelley series "Picket Fences" (1992–1996), a role that earned him an Emmy.

Tributes poured in from former co-stars. Julia Roberts, who played his daughter in "Steel Magnolias," wrote on Instagram: "A shining light of a gentle man. RIP." Kathy Baker, his "Picket Fences" co-star, called him "dear, lovely, loving Tom," and Lauren Holly remembered him as the show's leader: "His example made those years such a joy."

He is survived by his wife, Julie Tokashiki, five children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren. The family asked for privacy and said information about a memorial will be shared at a later date.

Sources: statement from Tom Skerritt's family to PEOPLE; Page Six.
